beats.title: The problem
beats.narration: Most of them get a shrug. The speaker in the kitchen can't see what she's pointing at. And little by little, the questions stop.

beats.title: Reveal
beats.narration: Meet Whyscope. A small companion for the biggest word in a child's vocabulary.

beats.title: It sees.
beats.narration: Point at anything. Whyscope looks with you.

beats.title: It answers like a kind grown-up.
beats.narration: It answers in seconds, in words a six-year-old already knows. Every fact comes from a knowledge base built for children.

beats.title: Then it asks you to guess.
beats.narration: And then it turns the question around. Guess first. Because the thinking is the point.

beats.title: It listens.
beats.narration: Hold the button and just ask. The listening happens right here, on the device.

beats.title: It knows what's for grown-ups.
beats.narration: Some questions belong to you. Whyscope hands them back gently, and gives you a few words to start with.

beats.title: For parents: a week of wonder.
beats.narration: Every week, a curiosity report. What she wondered about. Three things to talk about at dinner. Only the topics are kept. Never her voice, never her face.

beats.title: Everything stays home.
beats.narration: It runs on a two-and-a-half-watt chip, at home, without the cloud. No subscription. Nothing to switch off when a company disappears.

beats.title: Proof
beats.narration: Five numbers we will measure on the real hardware. Two of them, we already have.
